chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from 'Ubayd Allah al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in delaying al-maghrib during travel until the twilight disappears, and there is no harm in performing al-'atamah early during travel before the twilight disappears.

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the state of journeying that affects legal rulings
key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight glow whose disappearance marks a time boundary
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the maghrib prayer, the sunset salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُؤَخِّرَ: to delay the performance of the prayer
key_terms.يُعَجِّلَ: to perform earlier or advance in time

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a traveler to delay maghrib or perform 'isha before the twilight disappears?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the times of al-maghrib and al-'atamah during travel. It indicates flexibility for the traveler in delaying al-maghrib until the twilight disappears and in advancing al-'atamah before the twilight disappears.
